title: Psalms Chapter 34 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 34 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 34 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 34.

questions.question: In Psalms 34, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I will bless the LORD at all times
My soul shall make her boast in the LORD
O taste and see that the LORD is good
The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them
questions.correctAnswer: I will bless the LORD at all times
questions.explanation: This appears first in Psalms 34:1, where David declares his intent to bless the LORD at all times.

questions.question: What shall continually be in David's mouth according to Psalms 34?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:1 states that David's praise shall continually be in his mouth.

questions.question: Who shall hear David's boast in the LORD?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 34:2, the humble shall hear David's boast in the LORD and be glad.

questions.question: What does David invite others to do in Psalms 34:3?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 34:3, David invites others to magnify the LORD with him.

questions.question: What did David seek, and what was the result according to Psalms 34:4?
options: He sought wisdom and received it
He sought the LORD and He heard him
He sought riches and found them
He sought safety and was ignored
questions.correctAnswer: He sought the LORD and He heard him
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:4 states that David sought the LORD, and the LORD heard him and delivered him from all his fears.

questions.question: What happened to those who looked unto the LORD according to Psalms 34:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:5 says that they looked unto him and were lightened, and their faces were not ashamed.

questions.question: What did the poor man do in Psalms 34:6?
questions.explanation: The text in Psalms 34:6 states that this poor man cried, and the LORD heard him and saved him out of all his troubles.

questions.question: Who encampeth round about them that fear the LORD according to Psalms 34:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:7 states that the angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him and delivereth them.

questions.question: What is the man who trusteth in the LORD described as in Psalms 34:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:8 states that blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD.

questions.question: According to Psalms 34:4, what did the LORD deliver David from?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:4 indicates that the LORD delivered David from all his fears.

questions.question: What is the reaction of the humble to David's boast in the LORD?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 34:2, the humble shall hear David's boast in the LORD and be glad.

questions.question: The angel of the LORD delivers those who fear Him. True or False?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:7 confirms that the angel of the LORD delivers those that fear Him.

questions.question: David will bless the LORD at specific times. True or False?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:1 states that David will bless the LORD at all times, indicating a continuous action.

questions.question: The LORD saves those who are rich. True or False?
questions.explanation: The text does not state that the LORD saves the rich; rather, it mentions a poor man who cried and was saved (Psalms 34:6).

questions.question: David sought the LORD and found him in his troubles. True or False?
questions.explanation: The verse states that David sought the LORD and the LORD heard him, but it does not say he found Him; it emphasizes the LORD's hearing and delivering (Psalms 34:4).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 34 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 34 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is promised to those who fear the LORD according to Psalms 34:9?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:9 states that 'for there is no want to them that fear him.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 34:10 promise will happen if someone seeks the LORD?
options: They shall not want any good thing
They will be delivered from all troubles
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not want any good thing
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:10 states, 'but they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing.'

questions.question: What does David invite children to do in Psalms 34:11?
options: To hearken and learn the fear of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To hearken and learn the fear of the LORD
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:11 says, 'I will teach you the fear of the LORD.'

questions.question: What is the promise in Psalms 34:12 for those who desire life and good days?
options: They will be full of joy
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:12 asks, 'What man is he that desireth life, and loveth many days, that he may see good?' implying that seeing good is the outcome.

questions.question: What does Psalms 34:13 advise regarding speech?
options: To keep thy tongue from evil
To speak only good about others
questions.correctAnswer: To keep thy tongue from evil
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:13 explicitly instructs, 'Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.'

questions.question: What actions does Psalms 34:14 encourage?
options: Depart from evil and do good
questions.correctAnswer: Depart from evil and do good
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:14 commands, 'Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.'

questions.question: What is said about the eyes of the LORD in Psalms 34:15?
options: They are closed to the wicked
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:15 states, 'The eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 34:16 indicate about the face of the LORD?
options: It is against those who do evil
questions.correctAnswer: It is against those who do evil
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:16 states, 'The face of the LORD is against them that do evil.'

questions.question: How does Psalms 34:4 relate to the concept of fear of the LORD in Psalms 34:9?
options: Both call for praising the LORD
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:4 speaks of seeking the LORD and being delivered from fears, aligning with the security promised in Psalms 34:9 to those who fear Him.

questions.question: What connection can be made between Psalms 34:6 and Psalms 34:15?
options: Both affirm the LORD's attention to the righteous
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:6 speaks of the LORD saving the poor man out of his troubles, and Psalms 34:15 indicates the LORD's ears are open to the cries of the righteous, showing His attentiveness to deliver.

questions.question: What practical lesson can be drawn from Psalms 34:5 about trust in the LORD?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:5 suggests that those who look unto the LORD are lightened and not ashamed, implying that trust in Him results in joy and relief.

questions.question: What does Psalms 34:8 encourage people to do?
options: To taste and see that the LORD is good
questions.correctAnswer: To taste and see that the LORD is good
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:8 invites readers to experience the goodness of the LORD, saying, 'O taste and see that the LORD is good.'

questions.question: Is it true that the humble shall hear and be glad according to Psalms 34:2?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 34:2 states, 'the humble shall hear thereof, and be glad.'

questions.question: Is it false that the angel of the LORD encamps around the proud?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:7 states that 'The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him,' not the proud.

questions.question: Is it false that keeping one's tongue from evil is unnecessary?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 34:13 emphasizes the importance of keeping one's tongue from evil.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 34 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 34.

questions.question: What does the LORD do for the righteous when they cry out?
options: He hears them and delivers them
He is far away from them
questions.correctAnswer: He hears them and delivers them
questions.explanation: The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles. (Psalms 34:17)

questions.question: Who is the LORD close to according to Psalms 34?
questions.explanation: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit. (Psalms 34:18)

questions.question: What does Psalms 34:19 say about the afflictions of the righteous?
options: They are always delivered by the LORD
They are punished for their sins
They are greater than those of the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: They are always delivered by the LORD
questions.explanation: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all. (Psalms 34:19)

questions.question: According to Psalms 34:20, what is said about the bones of the righteous?
questions.explanation: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken. (Psalms 34:20)

questions.question: What will happen to those who hate the righteous according to Psalms 34:21?
questions.explanation: Evil shall slay the wicked: and they that hate the righteous shall be desolate. (Psalms 34:21)

questions.question: What does the term 'delivereth' in Psalms 34:17 mean?
questions.explanation: The term 'delivereth' refers to the act of rescuing from trouble, as seen in Psalms 34:17.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Psalms 34:18 when mentioning 'broken heart' and 'contrite spirit'?
questions.explanation: The phrases 'broken heart' and 'contrite spirit' reflect parallelism, a common literary device in Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of deliverance found in Psalms 34:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 41:10 echoes the theme of God's deliverance, promising that He will uphold and strengthen those who are fearful.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the promise of salvation for the broken-hearted found in Psalms 34:18?
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18 fulfills the promise of salvation for the broken-hearted, as Jesus proclaims His mission to heal and set free.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Psalms 34:19?
questions.explanation: The verse immediately before Psalms 34:19 is Psalms 34:18, stating 'The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart'.

questions.question: What comes immediately after Psalms 34:21?
options: The LORD redeemeth the soul of his servants
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD redeemeth the soul of his servants
questions.explanation: The verse immediately after Psalms 34:21 is Psalms 34:22, which states 'The LORD redeemeth the soul of his servants'.

questions.question: Psalms 34 teaches that the righteous will face many troubles, but what is their assurance?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:19 states, 'Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all'.

questions.question: The LORD's attentiveness to the cries of the righteous indicates what aspect of His character?
questions.explanation: The LORD's response to the cries of the righteous as mentioned in Psalms 34:17 shows His compassionate nature.

questions.question: The statement 'none of them that trust in him shall be desolate' is a promise in Psalms 34:22. Is this statement True or False?
questions.explanation: The verse promises that none who trust in the LORD shall be desolate, as stated in Psalms 34:22.

questions.question: The righteous are assured of deliverance from all their troubles. Is this statement True or False?
questions.explanation: While the righteous are assured of deliverance from many troubles, Psalms 34:19 specifies that they may still have many afflictions.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 34 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 34 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 34:4 teach about God's nature in relation to human fear?
options: God hears and delivers from all fears
God increases human fears to test faith
God only delivers the faithful from physical danger
questions.correctAnswer: God hears and delivers from all fears
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:4 states that God hears the supplicant and delivers him from all fears, demonstrating God's attentiveness and deliverance in the face of human anxiety.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 34:10 teach about God's provision for those who seek Him?
options: Those who seek the LORD shall not want any good thing
Provision is guaranteed only for the wealthy
God withholds good things to test patience
Provision is random and unrelated to seeking God
questions.correctAnswer: Those who seek the LORD shall not want any good thing
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:10 contrasts the young lions who suffer hunger with those who seek the LORD, who shall not lack any good thing, teaching God's faithful provision for His seekers.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in Psalms 34:13?
options: Believers must keep their tongues from evil and lips from guile
Sanctification is solely an external ritual
Speech has no bearing on holiness
Sinful speech is unavoidable for the sanctified
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must keep their tongues from evil and lips from guile
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:13 commands the control of speech from evil and deceit, emphasizing sanctification as active moral discipline involving words.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 34:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:7 describes the angel of the LORD encamping around those who fear Him to deliver them, illustrating God's protective care.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 34:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:18 states that the LORD is near to the brokenhearted and saves those of a contrite spirit, showing His compassionate nature.

questions.question: How does Psalms 34:22 connect to the New Testament doctrine of redemption?
options: It prefigures Christ's redeeming of the soul of His servants
It contradicts New Testament teaching on salvation by faith
It denies any future hope beyond this life
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ's redeeming of the soul of His servants
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:22 speaks of the LORD redeeming the soul of His servants, which is fulfilled and expanded in the New Testament teaching on Christ's redemptive work (cf. Ephesians 1:7).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Psalms 34:1–3 prepare for in the New Testament?
options: The continual praise of God by the redeemed community
The rejection of worship by humble believers
The cessation of praise after deliverance
The privatization of worship without community
questions.correctAnswer: The continual praise of God by the redeemed community
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:1–3 emphasizes blessing and magnifying the LORD at all times and together, prefiguring the New Testament theme of communal and continual praise in the body of Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 34:15 and 34:17 teach about God's relationship to the righteous?
options: God's attentiveness and deliverance in response to their cries
questions.correctAnswer: God's attentiveness and deliverance in response to their cries
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:15 notes that God's eyes and ears are attentive to the righteous, and 34:17 confirms that He hears their cries and delivers them, teaching God's responsive care.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 34:12 and 34:14 teach regarding the pursuit of life and holiness?
options: Desire for life is linked with departing from evil and doing good
Life is unrelated to moral behavior
Pursuit of peace contradicts desire for life
questions.correctAnswer: Desire for life is linked with departing from evil and doing good
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:12 asks who desires life and many days, and 34:14 commands departing from evil and doing good, linking sanctification with the blessing of life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 34:19 and 34:20 teach about the suffering and preservation of the righteous?
options: Though afflicted, the righteous are ultimately preserved intact by God
Righteousness guarantees a life free of affliction
Afflictions cause destruction of the righteous body
God abandons the righteous in suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Though afflicted, the righteous are ultimately preserved intact by God
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:19 acknowledges many afflictions of the righteous but 34:20 assures God keeps all their bones unbroken, showing divine preservation amid suffering.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 34:7–10 promises material prosperity to all believers, which is unrealistic. What does Psalms 34:7–10 actually teach?
options: God protects and provides for those who fear and seek Him, contrasting with the hungry young lions
God guarantees wealth and comfort to all believers regardless of their faithfulness
The passage teaches prosperity as a universal right without conditions
It teaches that believers will never face any hardships
questions.correctAnswer: God protects and provides for those who fear and seek Him, contrasting with the hungry young lions
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:7–10 emphasizes God's protection and provision for those who fear and seek Him, contrasting their sufficiency with the hunger of lions, indicating divine care rather than a blanket prosperity promise.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 34:21 teach about the fate of the wicked in relation to the righteous?
options: Evil will slay the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be desolate
The wicked prosper alongside the righteous
God is indifferent to the wicked's end
The righteous will be destroyed by their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Evil will slay the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be desolate
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:21 states that evil will slay the wicked and haters of the righteous will be desolate, teaching divine justice against evil opposed to the righteous.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Psalms 34:16 regarding God's stance toward evildoers?
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:16 shows God's face is against evildoers to erase their remembrance, highlighting His justice in opposing evil.

questions.question: How does Psalms 34:8 contribute to the theological understanding of experiential knowledge of God?
options: It invites believers to experience God's goodness firsthand
It dismisses sensory experience as irrelevant to faith
It insists on intellectual assent alone
It warns against tasting and seeing the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: It invites believers to experience God's goodness firsthand
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:8 says 'O taste and see that the LORD is good,' encouraging experiential knowledge of God's goodness as part of faith.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 34:2 and 34:9 teach about the relationship between humility, fear of the LORD, and spiritual satisfaction?
options: The humble and those who fear the LORD experience gladness and lack of want
Fear of the LORD leads to spiritual emptiness
Humility is unrelated to spiritual blessing
The proud are the truly blessed
questions.correctAnswer: The humble and those who fear the LORD experience gladness and lack of want
questions.explanation: Psalms 34:2 connects the humble hearing and being glad with 34:9's assurance that those who fear the LORD lack nothing, linking humility and reverence with blessing.
